title: 3D Printers Compared: Creality K2, K1 Max, Flashforge AD5X, LONGER LK10
metaDescription: Five fast 3D printers compared: LONGER LK10 and LK10 Plus, Flashforge AD5X, Creality K1 Max and K2 Combo, with build volume, speed, multicolor support and prices from $296.88 to $550.71.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: The five printers here share a price band, $296.88 to $550.71, and a speed-first design, but they split on one important question: do you want multicolor printing? The Creality K2 Combo and Flashforge AD5X are built for it, listing up to 16 and 4 colors. The LONGER LK10 and LK10 Plus are single-color machines with large build volumes, and the Creality K1 Max is a fast single-color printer. This is a head-to-head, and our general buying guide covers 3D printers in broader terms.

items.label: LONGER LK10 ($296.88)
items.value: 225x225x265 mm, 500 mm/s, 0.1 mm accuracy, auto leveling, dual Z-axis, 300 C hotend, WiFi/LAN/USB, PLA/PETG/ABS/ASA/TPU

items.label: LONGER LK10 Plus ($396.20)
items.value: 320x320x400 mm, 500 mm/s, same features plus a high-flow direct drive extruder

items.label: Creality K1 Max AI Speedy ($528.64)
items.value: Unicorn quick-swap nozzle; the listing does not give size or speed, so check the product page

items.label: Creality K2 Combo ($550.71)
items.value: CFS system, up to 16-color printing, 260x260x260 mm

pros: The LONGER LK10 at $296.88 is the cheapest here and still lists 500 mm/s, auto leveling and a 300 C hotend
The LK10 Plus has the largest build volume here (320x320x400 mm) for under $400
The AD5X offers 4-color printing for $318.95, only about $22 more than the LK10
The K2 Combo lists up to 16-color printing with a CFS system, the widest color range here
The LONGER listings state compatibility with PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA and TPU, a broad materials range
cons: The LK10 and LK10 Plus are single-color machines, so a multicolor model is needed for multi-color prints
The AD5X's 4-color capability and the K2's 16-color capability come with material waste and extra setup, which the listings do not quantify
The K1 Max listing is the vaguest, with no build volume or speed, so confirm specifications on its product page
The K2 Combo costs $550.71, about double the LK10, so you pay for color capability
Speed figures are maximums; real print time depends on the model, settings and print quality

items.question: Which printer should I buy if I only want single-color prints?
items.answer: The LONGER LK10 at $296.88 is the value choice. If you want to print larger objects, the LK10 Plus at $396.20 has a much bigger bed.

items.question: Is multicolor printing worth the extra money?
items.answer: Only if you want multi-colored prints without painting. The AD5X is the budget way in with 4 colors. The K2 Combo goes to 16 colors but costs about $230 more.

items.question: What happened to the K2 SE and other Creality models?
items.answer: The catalog changes often. The K2 Combo and K1 Max are the Creality printers listed at the moment.

items.question: Do I need an enclosure or filament dryer?
items.answer: For materials such as ABS and ASA, an enclosure helps, and a dryer keeps filament in good condition. The listings do not say whether either is included, so check each product page.

items.question: How fast are these printers really?
items.answer: The LONGER machines list 500 mm/s and the AD5X 600 mm/s as maximum speeds. Everyday print speeds are lower, especially for detailed models.

sections.content: Pick by color needs and size: the LK10 for the lowest price, the LK10 Plus for a big bed, the AD5X for affordable 4-color prints and the K2 Combo for the widest color range. Check the K1 Max page for specs the listing leaves out, and plan for filament and a dryer in your budget.
